entries.source: SDK 26.2, MPMediaPlaylist.h, @property (nonatomic, readonly, nullable) NSString *authorDisplayName MP_API(ios(9.3))
entries.reason: the release carries the accessor this is a convenience over and not the convenience: read with tools/mach32_methods.py from the armv7 cache of 6.1.3 (MediaPlayer image at 0x31fe3000), MPMediaPlaylist has 15 own instance methods and 3 own class methods and -valueForProperty: is among its own list; all 41 of the image's categories were read WITH THE CLASS EACH ONE EXTENDS, resolved through the category's own class pointer, and none extends MPMediaPlaylist, so nothing here can clobber the release's accessor and nothing in the release clobbers this one. -aSelectorNoFrameworkHas is absent as the control. The per-cache selector list does not decide a member - objectForKeyedSubscript: is on one line of it because a collection class declares it - which is the trap facts/MediaPlayer/MPMediaItem.md:105 records for albumTrackNumber. The KEY is Apple's and was read, not derived: MediaPlayerConstants93.m carries MPMediaPlaylistPropertyAuthorDisplayName = "externalVendorDisplayName", and facts/MediaPlayer/MediaPlayerConstants.md:8-12 records why that had to be read - ten of the thirteen MediaPlayer constants the port carries are dotted public.* strings and one holds the singular form of its own name, so a key spelled from the property's name would have been wrong twice
entries.effect: the value the release stores under Apple's key, and nil when that value is not an NSString. -valueForProperty: is typed id and the property is typed nullable NSString *, the release knows what it stored and the port cannot, so forwarding a wrong-typed value would hand a caller an object under a declaration that says NSString and the crash would arrive at the caller's first message to it
